A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Nemotron-CC research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, 8B-model training results at 1T and 15T tokens, and pipeline ablations in Tables 5–10 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original training results and ablations, including the appendix analyses of classifier overlap and quality buckets.

M1.justification: The extraction, three-classifier ensemble, quality bucketing, selective heuristic filtering and five synthesis prompts are retained. The new pipeline diagram, sampling parameters and deduplication details document the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Common Crawl snapshots, annotation data, English scope and evaluation tasks are unchanged. Auxiliary training coverage is ambiguous: v1 lists specialized math, whereas v2 omits it and newly identifies conversational data in Table 12. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects changed coverage or corrected documentation.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains FineWebEdu-2, FineWebEdu and DCLM; Table 6 retains Llama 3.1 8B. The extractor, classifier and synthetic-data comparisons in Tables 7–10 also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 revises the stated auxiliary training mix by dropping specialized math, while Table 12 identifies conversational data. This changes the reported setting without establishing reruns. The 73/27 split, model size, training budgets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the newly detailed curriculum documents the existing 15T-token experiment.

E4.justification: The extractor/filter, classifier and synthesis ablations are retained. The domain-overlap analysis and bucket comparison also remain unchanged, with the bucket plot moving from Figure 3 to Figure 4. The new contamination discussion contains no additional contamination experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results without repeated-seed summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-estimation practice or repeated-run count is added or revised.

E6.justification: v2 adds absolute bucket token counts to Table 2, including 553B high-quality and 2,023B medium-quality tokens, alongside the retained percentages. Section 2.2 corrects classifier recall from 'less than 10%' to 'around 10%', consistent with Table 9's retained 8% and 11%. Benchmark scores in Tables 5–10 are unchanged.

T1.justification: No theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation is added or revised. The score-bucketing and ensemble rules remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the delivered contributions from a released dataset and planned implementation to a reported release of the reference implementation and quality classifiers. The central accuracy, dataset-size and long-horizon suitability claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 newly explains why absolute high-quality token yield matters despite a lower high-quality fraction, and how bucketing controls the training mixture. Section 6 explicitly acknowledges the absence of decontamination and discusses its uncertain impact. Existing hallucination, diversity and English-only limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: it reports released reference code and classifier models, supplies classifier links and license information, specifies exact-substring deduplication over eighths of snapshots, and adds top-p 0.9 and temperature 0.5. Table 12 details the auxiliary blend, while Appendix E explains the existing 15T-token run's phases, mixture weights and quality selections.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cheng et al. (2024) on instruction pretraining and Feng et al. (2024) for the two-phase curriculum. Its principal positioning against FineWeb-Edu and DCLM is retained. Several other references receive publication metadata updates rather than representing additional cited works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v2 makes localized language corrections, expands explanations and acknowledgments, and adds pipeline-overview and curriculum appendices while renumbering the retained appendix material.

P2.justification: v2 adds the pipeline flowchart in Figure 3, the blend table in Table 12 and a token-count column in Table 2. It clarifies Table 7's caption and relocates retained figures, tables and prompt boxes. The overall two-column design and existing result displays remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is better transparency and reproducibility: v2 reports the previously promised implementation release, provides classifiers and synthesis settings, and explains the formerly underspecified 15T-token curriculum. Explicitly acknowledging undecontaminated data also improves qualification of the evidence. These benefits are limited by unchanged empirical validation, unmeasured contamination effects and ambiguity in the auxiliary-blend description.
